list.heading: Plugins
list.description: Your installed plugins, exactly as the Core reports them. Every plugin is untrusted by default: its capabilities are only what the Core explicitly, visibly, and revocably grants, and its manifest text and output are data — never instructions.
list.gateNote: The Plugin contract family is published and served by the Core, and the UI-29 trust/package gate was resolved by the owner's recorded decision: the install control below is live through an explicit package reference you supply, and the plugin detail's lifecycle controls are live behind their confirmations. No catalog exists (a catalog is supplied only by the Core — none is published), no local-package import is served (no served registry shape exists and the Core implements no validation + quarantine surface), and no invocation or execution surface exists (the D-13/D-14 gate and the Core Master Blueprint §10.2 runtime proof).
list.emptyAllBody: No user-installed plugin exists yet. The list renders only what the Core reports — no example plugin and no catalog is fabricated.
list.trustNote: Trust renders only what the Core returns: a trust state the Core does not return renders Unknown — never Verified. A digest match is not publisher trust; a signature is not proof of safe behavior; a downloaded source is not verified; a WASM sandbox label is not trust.
list.failureTitle: The plugin list could not be read
list.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the list read. Nothing was changed; the list stays empty until a confirmed read succeeds.
list.unknownTitle: The plugin list read did not return a usable answer
list.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof that the list is empty or that the read failed — refresh to read again.
list.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.

install.heading: Install a plugin package
install.inputNote: This install path is explicit, not a catalog: no catalog exists (a catalog is supplied only by the Core — none is published), so the package reference is one you supply yourself. The Core verifies and admits the package — the admission verdict is the Core's alone, and this surface performs no signature check, no digest computation for trust purposes, no manifest validation, and no compatibility determination of its own. A package you install is untrusted by default: its capabilities are only what the Core explicitly grants.
install.confirmScope: The Core will verify and admit the package, mint the plugin, package, install-record, and grant identities itself, and record the install. A confirmed install lands the plugin in its installed, not-yet-enabled state — enabling is a separate, confirmed act.
install.confirmLaws: Nothing is granted by installing: the plugin can never grant itself permissions; the granted set of record starts empty and changes only through explicit user grants that the Core mediates and enforces.
install.confirmedBody: The Core confirmed the install. The plugin landed in its installed, not-yet-enabled state; activation is separate, through the permission review on the plugin's detail page.
install.replayedBody: The Core returned the recorded install for this key — the same install record reference, never a second install.
install.unknownTitle: The install outcome is not known
install.unknownBody: The install response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof that the install succeeded or failed, and nothing is retried blindly: reconcile by the package identity through the authoritative reads before any further action.
install.reconcileFailed: The reconciliation read also did not return a usable answer. The uncertain state stays honestly labeled — check again after the Core answers.
install.emptyInput: Enter a package reference first — the reference is the Core's key to the package to verify and admit.
install.importAbsentBody: The published plugin family serves no import registry or package-upload shape, and the Core implements no validation + quarantine surface for local packages, so no import control exists here — the absence is the honest state, never a placeholder form.
install.catalogAbsentNote: No catalog surface exists: USER-INSTALLED is distinct from CATALOG-LISTED, always; a catalog exists only when the Core supplies one.

detail.gateNote: The UI-29 trust/package gate was resolved by the owner's recorded decision, so the lifecycle controls below are live behind their explicit two-step confirmations, and the permission-review structure rides activation. No invocation or execution surface exists (the D-13/D-14 gate and the Core Master Blueprint §10.2 runtime proof), and no catalog exists — the update's target reference has no served source to list versions from.
detail.executionGateNote: No invocation or execution surface exists: plugin execution is withheld by the D-13/D-14 gate, and the Core Master Blueprint §10.2 runtime proof stands unresolved. No invocation control, invocation state, or invocation-derived record is rendered here — nothing is invented for it.
detail.stateNote: This is the family's authoritative state endpoint (a pure query). Events are never the source of truth; this read is. A lost response on any lifecycle action reconciles here by the plugin/package identity — never by a timeout, never a local guess.
detail.actionsPendingNote: A lifecycle action is being confirmed by the Core. Other lifecycle actions stay unavailable until it resolves — duplicate submits are prevented, not queued.
detail.toggleTargetableNote: The enable/disable toggle operates on the installed, enabled, and disabled states only. A revoked state is not exitable through it: from grants revoked the Core refuses, and from trust revoked the Core refuses — re-granting or re-admission is your own explicit act through the Core's defined path.
detail.toggleShapeNote: The Core serves one state-toggle member covering both directions via its target state. A lost response reconciles through the authoritative state read before any retry — never a local flip, never an optimistic state change.
detail.enableConfirmScope: Enabling is activation — a high-risk action confirmed explicitly. The Core confirms the state change and records it; a plugin you enable is still untrusted by default, and its capabilities remain only what the Core explicitly, visibly, and revocably grants.
detail.enableConfirmReviewLaws: The permission review that gates enabling is per-permission and explicit: you grant or deny each requested capability yourself, the data-egress description renders before anything is granted, and Escape or Cancel cancels the review — no implied grant, no implied deny. The plugin can never grant itself permissions; the Core mediates and enforces.
detail.enableConfirmReviewAbsent: On this Core no requested-capability record is served (the manifest member is absent on the served record), so the review's per-permission items cannot render — the absence is the honest state, never a fabricated review item. The Core's own admission and authorization still govern activation: a policy denial blocks it and is surfaced as the Core's typed refusal.
detail.disableConfirmScope: Disabling is your action, distinct from grants revoked and from trust revoked — neither revocation is implied or performed. The Core confirms the state change and records it; the plugin's granted set of record is untouched by this action as far as the Core reports.
detail.updateTargetNote: No served surface lists available target versions (no catalog exists and no version-list member is served), so the target reference is one you supply explicitly. The Core verifies the target: an unresolvable target is the Core's typed refusal, and nothing here fabricates or guesses a target value.
detail.updateConfirmScope: The update switches the plugin to the target version reference you supplied. The prior version keeps running until the Core confirms the switch (the atomic upgrade — no artifact overwrite while an old active plugin runs), and the lifecycle state, granted set, and install record are preserved as the Core reports them.
detail.updateConfirmFreshReview: Any permission change triggers a fresh review of the changed set before the update may complete: changed capabilities are never silently widened, and the Core's typed refusal stores nothing — a retry never grants.
detail.removeConfirmScope: Removal is a high-risk action confirmed explicitly. The Core confirms the removal; disposal follows the Core's retention — no erasure claim is made beyond the Core-confirmed scope, and the keyed operation record persists for the replay window so a lost response's retry reconciles the recorded outcome.
detail.removeConfirmOpenNote: Whether removing a plugin and revoking its grants are the same or distinct effects is recorded OPEN — the Core's contract decides. This confirmation asserts neither, and no copy here promises either answer.
detail.revokeConfirmScope: Revoking is your explicit high-risk act on the plugin's capabilities: revocation blocks future invocations, and the current invocation's behavior is reported by the Core — never guessed (on this Core no invocation path exists while the execution rows are gated, so there is no current invocation to report).
detail.revokeConfirmLaw: The granted set of record is emptied and the lifecycle state moves to grants revoked — distinct from disabled and from trust revoked. A retry never re-grants, and a denial stands until your own explicit act.
detail.emptyInput: Enter the required reference first — the Core needs it to identify what this action applies to.
detail.replayedNote: The keyed replay returned the recorded outcome — the same Core-confirmed result, never a second mutation.
detail.removedBody: The Core confirmed the removal. The artifact is absent from the user-installed list per the Core; re-install goes through the install path on the plugin list.
detail.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof of success, failure, or safe retry: reconcile through the authoritative state read before any further action — no blind retry is offered.
detail.unknownNoKeyNote: No request reference rides this member: the served state-toggle body carries exactly one member (the target state), so the reconcile goes through the authoritative state read alone.
detail.reconcileFailed: The reconciliation read also did not return a usable answer. The uncertain state stays honestly labeled with its reference — check again after the Core answers.
detail.actionFailureBody: The Core refused the action and nothing was changed by it. The refusal's typed code is shown verbatim; nothing here retries blindly — proceed through the Core's defined path.
detail.overviewDistinctNote: The lifecycle states are distinct and stay distinct: Disabled (your action) is not Grants revoked, Grants revoked is not Trust revoked, and Trust revoked is not either — each renders its own state, never merged, never shown as a milder one. A failure state is never shown as a user-action state, and a user action is never shown as a failure.
detail.overviewTrustNote: Verified, Trusted, and Installed appear only after the corresponding Core evidence and policy conditions are met. This surface renders Core-returned values only — an absent verification state is never rendered as a verified one, and a trust state the Core does not return renders Unknown, never Verified.
detail.overviewFailureNote: The typed failure states (quota-terminated, crash, compatibility failure, trust revocation) render only as the Core returns them, never computed here. On this Core no invocation path exists (the execution gate) and no admission verification machinery is wired, so no failure record is producible — the absence is the honest state, never a fabricated failure.
detail.manifestAbsentTitle: The Core serves no manifest for this record
detail.manifestAbsentBody: The manifest member is optional on the published plugin record, and no manifest-examination path exists on this Core, so the served record carries none. The manifest fields (manifest version, plugin identity and version, publisher reference, artifact digest and signature, ABI version, requested capabilities, compatibility range, declared resource needs, license/SBOM reference, lifecycle state) render here exactly as the Core returns them once a served manifest exists — no manifest is fabricated.
detail.manifestUntrustedNote: Manifest text is untrusted data: rendered, never executed. It cannot grant permissions, mint capabilities, or change system instructions, and no plugin-supplied content executes in any rendered surface here.
detail.manifestResourceNote: The surface displays only Core-returned, proven limits where any limit is shown: per-instruction CPU/fuel quota is not assumed, and a wall-clock timeout is not fuel — a declared resource need is a declaration, and the Core's enforcement is the only authority.
detail.capabilitiesAbsentTitle: No granted-capability record is served here
detail.capabilitiesAbsentBody: The served record carries no granted-capability member, and no capability catalogue is published (the capability class rides the family only). The granted set of record starts empty at install and changes only through the Core's own acts — nothing is invented here.
detail.capabilitiesNeverGrantNote: A plugin can never grant itself permissions: the user grants and denies, and the Core mediates and enforces. Every grant is explicit, scoped, revocable, and auditable; a declared capability name is data, never a grant.
detail.capabilitiesReviewNote: The permission-review flow rides activation: it renders inside the enable confirmation, per-permission and explicit, with the data-egress description shown before anything is granted and Escape cancelling without implying either. On this Core no requested-capability record is served (the manifest member is absent), so the review renders its honest absence there — the Core's own admission and authorization still govern activation.
detail.compatibilityAbsentTitle: No compatibility record is served here
detail.compatibilityAbsentBody: The Core serves no ABI or compatibility result for this record: the manifest member is absent (so no declared ABI version or compatibility range is served) and the Core returns no compatibility determination. The mismatch and update availability render here where the Core reports them — never computed.
detail.compatibilityAbiNote: The plugin's ABI version is separate from the host capability version; the Core's compatibility check is authoritative, an unknown required capability is rejected Core-side, and this surface performs no compatibility determination of its own.
detail.digestNoPackageTitle: No package record is served here
detail.digestNoPackageBody: The served record carries no package member, so no package verification state renders. The package verification states render exactly as the Core returns them once a served package exists — never computed, never inferred.
detail.digestVerificationNote: Every verification state here is Core-returned and rendered as returned: an absent member renders Unavailable and is never presented as verified. On this Core the served package carries the package reference alone — no verification machinery is wired — so the verification members render their honest absence.
detail.digestTrustWordNote: A digest establishes content identity relative to compared bytes only — never publisher authorization, authenticity, safety, or factual truth. A signature is not proof of safe behavior. A WASM sandbox label is defense in depth, not the trust boundary: the Core's authorization is. Trust revoked is distinct from Disabled and from Grants revoked, wherever the Core reports it.
detail.logsAbsentTitle: No sanitized diagnostics are served here
detail.logsAbsentBody: No published member serves plugin diagnostics for this family yet, so no log content renders. Missing and unavailable diagnostics are labeled honestly — nothing is reconstructed or substituted.
detail.logsRedactionNote: Redaction is the Core's duty; this surface never displays unredacted raw output. What may never appear here: secret values of any kind (a named secret-handle's name only, never its value), raw logs, runtime internals, stack traces, or memory contents, raw plugin output or raw provider payloads as diagnostics, and any diagnostic the Core did not return.
detail.auditAbsentTitle: No plugin event record is served here
detail.auditAbsentBody: The plugin family's lifecycle events ride the Core's audit layer, and no published member serves them on this surface. The Activity & Audit destination renders the audit categories it is served — this tab renders nothing invented.
detail.auditSourceNote: Events are never the source of truth: the authoritative state endpoint above is. The Core's audit receipts ride the Core's audit layer — this surface mints no parallel journal.
detail.failureTitle: The plugin record could not be read
detail.failureBody: The Core refused or could not answer the plugin read. Nothing was changed; the page stays empty until a confirmed read succeeds.
detail.unknownTitle: The plugin read did not return a usable answer
detail.unknownBody: The response was lost or could not be interpreted. A lost response is never proof of any outcome — refresh to read again.
detail.connectionHint: Check that the Core is running, then refresh.
detail.notFoundTitle: No plugin answers to this address
detail.notFoundBody: The Core's typed refusal answers unknown and out-of-scope identities with the same response — existence is never inferred from a refusal. Go back to the plugin list and open a plugin from there.
